ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against: (1) French PEP list maintained by ACPR and TRACFIN; (2) EU Sanctions Map and EU Consolidated List; (3) UN Security Council Consolidated List; (4) OFAC SDN and SSI lists; (5) French national freeze register (Registre national des gels) managed by DG Trésor; (6) World Bank Debarred Firms. Enhanced due diligence (EDD) required for high-risk jurisdictions and PEPs under Article L.561-10 CMF. Screening must be refreshed every 90 days. Gaming sector (ISIC 5820) classified as Low_Risk_Standard under French AML typologies, but enhanced scrutiny applies to Steam and PlayStation payout corridors.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Infogreffe (https://www.infogreffe.fr) and INPI (Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle) trademark database for name availability verification
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: French language mandatory for corporate name under Article L.123-1 of Commercial Code. Use of French script required. Foreign characters must be transliterated into Latin script. Non-French terms permitted only if accompanied by French translation or if exceptionally authorized by ministerial decree. Name must not be misleading or contrary to public policy.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection by INPI or Greffe, applicant may file an administrative appeal (recours gracieux) with INPI within 15 days of notification. If rejected, file appeal with Paris Court of Appeal (Cour d'appel de Paris) within one month under Article L.411-4 of the Intellectual Property Code. For Greffe-based rejection, appeal to the local Commercial Court (Tribunal de commerce). Legal counsel recommended. Concurrent trademark clearance search is mandatory to avoid infringement claims.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual offices are not accepted as registered office for SAS entities engaged in video game publishing under ISIC 5820. A physical commercial lease (bail commercial), domiciliation agreement with a domiciliation company authorized by the Prefecture, or own premises is required. Article L.123-11 of Commercial Code permits domiciliation only through authorized entities. Digital publishing activity may qualify for domiciliation at a professional domiciliation provider, but physical substance is increasingly required by tax authorities for transfer pricing and permanent establishment analysis.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Medium-High (approximately 45-60% within first 18 months for newly incorporated entities in digital publishing sector). French tax authority (DGFiP) conducts unannounced verifications under Article L.10 of Book of Tax Procedures (Livre des procédures fiscales). Social security authority (URSSAF) and labor inspectorate may also conduct physical inspections. Physical presence and commercial substance documentation recommended from day one.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP); portal: impots.gouv.fr; formalities via Guichet Unique (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr); non-resident filings with SIE Non-Résidents
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Domestic SAS: file formation via Guichet Unique; INPI/RCS allocates SIREN (9 digits) and SIRET (14 digits); DGFiP issues TVA intracommunautaire number FR+key+SIREN. Non-established foreign entities: file VAT registration form CERFA n° 15681*01 with SIE Non-Résidents; non-EU entities must appoint an approved fiscal representative (représentant fiscal agréé). Attach certificate of tax residence, notarized articles (French translation), power of attorney, and proof of first French taxable transaction; number issued within 30 days.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box; the SAS cannot elect pass-through taxation. Available elections: 95% French tax consolidation (CGI art. 223 A), VAT group (CGI art. 256 C quinquies), participation-exemption (mère-fille), rollover/merger elections for intellectual-property gains; ATAD II hybrid-mismatch notifications and documentation are mandatory filings.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (TVA) under the Code Général des Impôts and EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: None - EUR 0; registration from the first taxable French transaction. The small-business exemption (CGI art. 293 B) applies only to French-established SMEs with annual turnover below EUR 36,800 (services) / EUR 91,000 (goods); the EU cross-border B2C OSS convenience threshold is EUR 10,000 annually.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory structured e-invoicing for domestic B2B: 1 Sep 2026 (large/mid-size) and 1 Sep 2027 (SMEs); 'Y' model with certified PDPs and the Public Facturation Portal (PPF) via API; formats Factur-X/UBL/CII. No real-time tax-clearance stamp; B2C e-reporting transmitted periodically to DGFiP. Platform payments from Steam/PlayStation should be matched in VAT returns and OSS declarations; penalties under CGI arts. 1737/1737 ter.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exports outside the EU qualify for 0% VAT (CGI arts. 262-1, 269). The main publishing flow is a B2B service to Valve/PlayStation (merchant of record outside France), so the place of supply is the customer's establishment (CGI art. 259 A) and no French VAT is due. Direct B2C sales to consumers outside the EU/EU are handled under CGI art. 259 B: no French VAT on non-EU consumers; EU consumers via OSS at destination rates. Export zero-rating does not apply to digital services; territoriality exclusion is the operative mechanism and requires geolocation evidence.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DAU via DELTA-X) - only for physical media/merchandise exports; digital-only supplies do not require export declarations
Bill of Lading/CMR/Airway Bill - for physical goods or promotional inventories consigned to non-EU customers
Inward Remittance Certificate and bank statement - evidencing collection of platform payouts and foreign-exchange repatriation

Digital substantiation set - Steam/PlayStation payout reports, IP and BIN geolocation records, billing addresses, and licensing contracts establishing customer location and the merchant-of-record model
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGFiP digital-economy audits cross-match platform payout data with VAT returns and OSS filings; unsubstantiated zero-rating or out-of-scope claims are re-assessed at 20% VAT with monthly interest (CGI art. 1727) and penalties of 40% (bad-faith) or 80% (organized fraud) under CGI art. 1729, plus denial of deductible-input VAT. Customs false-declaration sanctions under the Code des Douanes may reach 3 years' imprisonment and confiscation of goods. The standard audit limitation period is 3 years (extended to 10 years in cases of hidden offshore activities), and refund claims are subject to retrospective clawback where customer geolocation evidence is proven inaccurate.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France operates a fully convertible Eurozone capital account regime under Banque de France oversight. Capital account transactions above EUR 100,000 per transaction or EUR 1 million annually for residents require prior declaration via FICO. Profit remittances face no convertibility restrictions but are subject to French withholding taxes (12.8% on interest, 30% on dividends), transfer pricing compliance, and beneficial ownership verification. Hurdles include economic substance justification and annual tax reporting.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory surrender of export proceeds to the central bank. French exporters retain and repatriate foreign exchange freely at market rates. All transactions require customs declarations and statistical reporting to INSEE. For digital publishing via Steam and PlayStation stores, USD payouts must be converted to EUR through licensed French banks with full documentation for VAT (20%) and corporate tax purposes.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Fintech EMI cross-border viability is moderate under French PSD2 and TRACFIN regulations. Offshore digital EMIs require local banking partnerships for Steam and PlayStation payouts; direct offshore accounts face heightened AML scrutiny and may be restricted for corporate entities.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote KYC via video and digital documents is permitted for standard French SAS corporate onboarding. Physical presence is not mandatory for accounts under EUR 1 million but required for higher-value or high-risk transactions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity or shell company indicators
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Ultimate beneficial owner declaration, corporate structure chart, source of wealth documentation, and notarized power of attorney

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctioned jurisdiction links or adverse media
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Enhanced due diligence report, transaction history, legal opinions confirming legitimacy, and beneficial ownership certificate

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound wires use SWIFT MT103 with purpose codes 'CAP' for capital contributions or 'EQTY' for equity injections. French banks require IBAN validation, beneficial ownership verification via KYC, and supporting documents such as share subscription agreements. Verification matches against corporate records and tax filings.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements cleared via SWIFT MT103 for direct payments or Commercial Letters of Credit (LC) under UCP 600 for trade settlements. For digital publishing royalties, direct payouts to Steam and PlayStation store accounts are permissible with proper invoicing and VAT handling.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Shareholder adoption of annual financial statements (décision d'affectation des résultats) of the SAS
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Not filed; documented in the company's statutory minute book / share register (internal corporate record)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six (6) months of fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Exposure to court action by any interested party to compel approval; possible civil liability of the president; risk of administrative strike-off upon persistent non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of annual accounts (comptes annuels) including balance sheet, income statement, notes, and appointments of the SAS with the commercial registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Commercial Court Registry), filed electronically via the INPI Guichet Unique / Registre National des Entreprises (RNE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one (1) month after shareholder approval; maximum seven (7) months after fiscal year-end for calendar-year companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Civil fine up to EUR 1,500 (EUR 3,000 on repeat default) plus court-ordered coercive penalty (astreinte); registry may flag the company as non-compliant and the Kbis extract may be restricted.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (déclaration de résultats) – form 2065 and supporting schedules (liasse fiscale)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) – French Tax Authorities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three (3) months of fiscal year-end; for calendar-year fiscal year, electronic filing due generally on the second business day after 1 May (i.e., 2 or 3 May)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest at 0.40% per month plus a surcharge of 5% or 10% on assessed corporate income tax; potential loss of tax-reduction attributes.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual local business contribution (Cotisation Foncière des Entreprises – CFE) returns and payment for the SAS
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (local tax office)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual payment no later than 15 December; declaration of business property (form 1447-C) generally due by the second business day after 1 May for the absence of business premises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% late-payment surcharge plus late interest; execution of tax liability may be enforced against the SAS's assets.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Statutory audit (commissaire aux comptes) is mandatory for an SAS when it exceeds at any closing date two of the three French legal thresholds: balance-sheet total of EUR 4,000,000; net operating revenue of EUR 8,000,000; average number of employees of 50. Audit also may be required on request of shareholders, creditors, or the public prosecutor even below thresholds, and if the SAS is a parent or controlled entity required to file consolidated accounts.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Individual annual accounts must be prepared in accordance with French generally accepted accounting principles (PCG – Plan Comptable Général); listed companies or consolidated financial statements must apply IFRS as endorsed by the EU.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: French AML law does not impose a regular annual UBO declaration. The initial declaration (déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs) must be filed at incorporation and within 60 days of any change in beneficial ownership. As part of the annual secretarial cycle, the SAS should review its UBO file alongside the annual accounts; no separate annual confirmation is due if the data remains unchanged.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Registre des mouvements de titres et actions (Register of Members / Share Transfer Register)
Registre des dirigeants (Register of Directors and Officers), kept for internal governance consistency with RCS filings
Registre des décisions et procès-verbaux (Minute Book of Non-binding Decisions and General Meeting Records)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (standard IS rate applicable from fiscal years beginning on or after 1 January 2022)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 15% rate on the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit for qualifying SMEs (turnover ≤ EUR 10M, 75% owned by individuals); research tax credit (CIR) at 30% (2023) on eligible R&D; innovation tax credit (CII); video game creation tax credit (CIJV) up to 30% of eligible production expenses capped at EUR 3M per year (EUR 6M for certain games)
